brief.headline: Offer to pay in 15 days instead of 30 and ask for a 6–7% price cut in return — their cash is stuck for 101 days, much longer than similar firms (64 days), so faster payment is worth that much to them.

priceAsk.summary: Ask for a 6–7% price cut if we pay in 15 days instead of 30
priceAsk.target: Around 6–7% saving (roughly their borrowing cost of 12.16% halved for 15 days early payment)
priceAsk.basis: Their cash is stuck for 101 days vs 64 days for similar firms, and they borrow money at about 12.16% — so paying 15 days early is worth roughly 6–7% to them. The market ask for pharma/ORS sachet laminate is ₹205–305/kg (typical ₹250/kg), which the data labels 'MARKET-FAIR (top of fair band)' — so there's room to move down within that band.

paymentTermAsk.summary: Offer to pay in 15 days (half our current 30 days) in exchange for the price cut
paymentTermAsk.cashImpact: ₹26.60 L of cash freed up for us by moving from 30-day to 15-day terms

brief.financialLeverage: They make ₹1064.86 Cr a year and keep only 2.3% as profit — very tight margins, so a big price squeeze could hurt supply. But their cash is stuck for 101 days, much longer than similar firms (64 days), and they owe ₹282.62 Cr (1.25 times their own cash), so cash is tight for them. We're only 0.61% of their revenue (₹6.47 Cr), so we're a small customer — but they'll value faster payment because it shortens that 101-day cash wait. Their credit rating is CARE BBB+ / Stable and they're in the 'grey' distress zone (Altman Z = 2.36), plus they've had EPF payment delays — so push firmly on payment-for-discount, but don't squeeze so hard you tip a fragile supplier over.

evidence.point: Their cash is stuck for 101 days, vs 64 days for similar firms — so cash is tight
They borrow at about 12.16%, so paying early is worth that rate to them
They keep only 2.3% as profit — very little room to cut price without hurting them
They owe 1.25 times their own cash, and total debt is ₹282.62 Cr
We're only 0.61% of their ₹1064.86 Cr revenue, so we're a small customer
The market ask for pharma/ORS sachet laminate is ₹205–305/kg (typical ₹250/kg), verdict: MARKET-FAIR (top of fair band)

alternates.why: Global Constantia group's India converter for pharma blister/sachet laminates — strong second-source option (revenue ₹222.04 Cr, health D 31/100)

risks: Their credit rating is CARE BBB+ / Stable and Altman Z is 2.36 ('grey' distress zone) — watch supply stability; don't squeeze so hard you tip them over
They've had EPF payment delays — a red flag on financial discipline; qualify a second source now
We're only 0.61% of their revenue, so we have limited bargaining power on price alone — the payment-for-discount swap is our strongest lever
Profit margin is only 2.3% — a big price cut could hurt their ability to deliver consistently; keep the ask realistic (6–7%, not 15%)
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We'd like to help free up cash for you by paying in 15 days instead of 30 — in return, we're looking for a 6–7% price reduction to share the benefit.
